newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close flat, Ssangyong shares mixed.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close flat, Ssangyong shares mixed.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed Wednesday slightly lower as anticipation of an inflow of a large amount of foreign funds fizzled out, brokers said.
The foreign holding limit of Korean stocks will rise to 23 percent from 20 percent on Friday. The market will be closed on Thursday.
Ssangyong Group shares ended mixed after the nation's sixth largest conglomerate announced a business restructuring plan, they said.
But Tuesday's rally on Wall Street had no impact on Seoul.
The composite stock index shed 0.82 of a point to 703.23.
"The market is expected to repeat the past pattern on Friday with foreigners buying and domestic institutions unloading their holdings," said Kim Myung-ho of Hyundai Securities.
Brokers forecast about 500 billion won would flow in after the ceiling expansion but at a gradual pace. They said the amount is far short of the market anticipation.
Blue chips lost ground on domestic institutional selling. SK Telecom lost 1,500 won to 456,000 and POSCO shed 500 won to 53,600.
Ssangyong Group said it would curtail its affiliates to 21 from the current 25 to sharpen its competitiveness.
The group said Ssangyong Heavy Industries Co would absorb Ssangyong Precision Industry Co.
Analysts said the move was aiming at saving loss-making Ssangyong Motor. But the carmaker went limit down, losing 450 won to 5,290.
"The move failed to impress investors as it's not big enough to salvage the auto manufacturer," said an LG Securities analyst.
Analysts said financial problems of the Ssangyong Group surfaced after Ssangyong Motor said it would sell its assets to raise about 400 billion won.
They said the trouble had been reflected in the group shares with seven of the 10 listed Ssangyong Group shares trading at below 10,000 won.
"The market will not react positively unless the group comes up with more concrete steps to generate money," Kim said.
Ha Seung-hoon of Jardine Fleming said investors are worried about the possibility of margin loans outpacing customer deposits at brokerage houses.
But he said signs of improvement in economic indicators released on Tuesday limited sharp falls on the index.

Industrial output in March rose 9.1 percent year-on-year, up from a 5.8 percent rise a year earlier. The current account deficit widened to $2.27 billion in March from $940.2 million a year ago, but narrowed from February's $2.50 billion deficit.
Anam Industrial Corp recorded Wednesday's largest trading volume with 807,370 shares changing hands. It briefly hit a 1997 high of 14,000 won, but closed at 13,500, up 500.
Brokers attributed the rise to anticipation of a jump in the company's earnings this year. But a company official said profits would worsen this year on heavy facilities investment.
-- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
